s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive back pain and bilateral leg weakness with evidence of spinal injury
salient_findings: L5 burst fracture with canal compromise
key_facts: 28-year-old man
Uses a wheelchair
Severe back pain for two weeks
Mild back pain after pulling a rug one month earlier
Progressive bilateral leg weakness
Diffuse paresthesia
History of bodybuilding with use of licensed and unlicensed substances
No significant trauma
Severe left and moderate right weakness of the extensor hallucis longus muscles
Moderate weakness of ankle dorsiflexors bilaterally
Normal quadriceps and ankle plantarflexion strength
Intact sphincter function
Elevated C-reactive protein level
L2 compression fracture
L5 burst fracture with canal compromise and intravertebral vacuum cleft
T2-weighted "double line sign" at L5 on MRI

shortlist.label: Kummell disease
shortlist.why_kept: Intravertebral vacuum cleft and vertebral compression fracture

shortlist.label: Vertebral osteonecrosis
shortlist.why_kept: T2-weighted "double line sign" at L5 on MRI

shortlist.label: Spondylolisthesis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral leg weakness and diffuse paresthesia with spinal injury

shortlist.label: Spinal tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein level and spinal injury

raw.rationale: The presence of an intravertebral vacuum cleft and a "double line sign" on MRI are characteristic of Kummell disease, a subtype of osteoporotic vertebral fractures.

rejected.label: Osteoporosis
rejected.why: Too broad, as it does not specifically account for the intravertebral vacuum cleft and "double line sign"

rejected.label: Vertebral osteonecrosis
rejected.why: Not supported by the presence of a "double line sign" and intravertebral vacuum cleft, which are more characteristic of Kummell disease

rejected.label: Spondylolisthesis
rejected.why: Not indicated by the presence of a compression fracture and burst fracture without evidence of vertebral slippage

rejected.label: Spinal tuberculosis
rejected.why: Not supported by the lack of paravertebral soft-tissue mass or abscess and the absence of other systemic symptoms of infection
